summary: Node mTLS certificate renewal on the myseliasan fleet control plane is now operator-gated per node instead of renewing automatically and silently forever. A new ManagedNode.AutoRenew flag (default off for newly adopted nodes) must be enabled by an operator, via a new toggle on the node's Details tab or PUT /api/nodes/{id}/auto-renew, before the control plane's Enroll endpoint will honour a renewal re-enrollment from that node (the node still authenticates with its existing pairing token and needs no claim code; only the control plane's willingness to sign changed). Initial enrollment right after adoption is never gated. A node whose operator never turns this on simply lets its certificate lapse on schedule, drops off the control channel, and goes lost -- a per-node dead-man's switch so a forgotten or decommissioned node falls out of the fleet without anyone having to remember to explicitly revoke it. The fleet-health 'certificate expiring' warning now fires only for nodes with auto-renew off (an auto-renew-on node's renewal will be honoured, so its approaching expiry is not actionable). Node certificate default lifetime was raised from 7 to 90 days (pairing.certTtlHours, shipped config.json now sets 2160) so an un-renewed node stays reachable for a meaningful window, and the control-plane cert-expiry warning window (pairing.renewBeforeHours) was raised to 336 hours (14 days) in the shipped config to match.
compatibility: Upgrading an existing installation does not silently expire any currently-adopted node: a one-time startup pass (INodeRegistry.BackfillAutoRenew, guarded by a persisted pairing.autoRenewBackfilled control setting) turns auto-renew on for every node that was already enrolled before this feature shipped, preserving the old always-renews behavior for them. Only nodes adopted after upgrading start with auto-renew off and require an explicit operator opt-in to keep renewing past their first certificate. No claim code or re-adoption is needed to enable it. Existing config.json deployments keep their configured certTtlHours/renewBeforeHours unless updated; the shipped defaults changed (168h to 2160h TTL, and the shipped config's renewBeforeHours to 336h) but a 0/unset value still falls back to the new built-in defaults.
